ItemData.Value: Butterfly inserted but blood seeping around sides of device. Good compression but uterus clearly well contracted -felt easily with device in place. So device removed and moved immediately to repair of posterior vaginal wall repair and main source of bleeding from bilateral cervical tears.
Liked that it was diagnostic-saved time and avoided going to theatre
No problems with use. Inserted with ease, initially noted to be mildly uncomfortable once in position. Removed with ease.
I found it difficult to assess active loss possibly due to my position ,should have been higher /better position of myself.
That it wasn't a 'hand'-size and personal aspects
Well tolerated. Pudendal analgesia only. Very easy to use.
Episiotomy,Forceps delivery.Sutures in Rectum ,removed and resutured.Treated as a 3rd degree tear (laxatives,antibiotics and follow up)
Calmness,confidence of staff using the device.
The woman did not even notice when it was inserted. It is unclear whether it was the Oxytocin bolus or the Butterfly that worked.

The uterus was atonic following the Syntocinon bolus (I had performed massage but had not explored the cavity). I inserted the Butterfly, gave pressure and the bleeding stopped. I released the pressure after 3 minutes and the bleeding stayed stopped. I removed the Butterfly but a trickle restarted, I evacuated clots from the uterus and the bleeding stopped.
Entrapment of Anterior vaginal wall and labia after opening the wings of the device. No trauma was caused but there was the potential for trauma if care had not been taken.
Jehovah's witness (declined all blood products). In the future I would not open the wings of the device as this caused the Anterior vaginal wall to become caught.
Prolonged inpatient stay due to dural tap following epidural
Saw the device afterwards which was abit daunting,wouldn't have liked to see it prior to it being used.
Post epidural Dural Tap requiring Blood patch.
Saw the instrument/device after the clinician used it
That I didn't see the device before use
That it's called a 'Butterfly',image of something small and delicate.
Seemed like a better alternative to a hand.

This lady had a severe uterine atony after delivery of the placenta. I estimate she bled 500 ml in under 60 seconds, the uterine tone did not improve with massage and she had no IV access. I performed Bimanual Compression while we established IV access, gave uterotonics and I consented for the PPH Butterfly. The patient was much more comfortable with the PPH Butterfly than the Bimanual and it gave good compression to stop the bleeding while the Carboprost took effect.
That it was an instrument rather than a hand-depersonalises the procedure.
Repair of 2nd degree tear that was bleeding.
Straightforward to use. Quite comfortable for patient when in place, only having a small amount of loss at the time the Butterfly was used but it did seem to help with the bleeding.
It appeared to sort the problem out

The Butterfly device was useful in assessing the origin of postpartum haemorrhage (i.e. upper genital tract), and assessing severity of on going haemorrhage. The device also facilitated effective uterine compression.
The size of the box was alarming.
Patient commented specifically that Butterfly was more comfortable than Bimanual Compression. Patient didn't appear to feel any discomfort on insertion, pressure or removal.
Saw the device beforehand which was frightening,but the doctor explained that it was only 'part' of the device (and showed it to her) that would be inserted.
Had Bimanual Compression first so this was preferable.

Patient had on going steady uterine bleeding from placental bed, despite medical treatment and use of PPH Butterfly device to aid Bimanual Compression. We therefore proceeded to insertion of Bakri Balloon to enable uterine tamponade.
Patient attendance post discharge with perineal breakdown and infection.
The woman commented that she preferred the Butterfly to Bimanual compression as it was less invasive, even after she had manual exploration of the uterine cavity.
It looked a bit big,can it be smaller?
The plastic made it look cheap.
I am very sorry, I inserted this whilst pt. was under GA. I got verbal consent pre-GA,I forgot in the heat of the moment that this was an exclusion criteria.
participant admitted into hospital within 6 weeks of delivery. Suspected sepsis: examiniation revealed retained products, evacuated
Not able to comment as pt. was under GA
Not able to comment as pt. was under GA.

Gave birth 22/05/2018. Attended 18/06 with heavy lochia, seen on MAU and discharged. Re-attended 20/06/2018 with infection/sepsis, admitted for treatment from 20/06/2018 to 25/06/2018. USS revealed retained products, had uterine evacuation.Due to be followed up on 10/07/2018 but DNA; no response to phone calls-discharged.
No implications for safety of study participants. C.I. assessment: Causality-Unrelated Severity-Moderate
Haemabate 250 mcg IM x 2,EUA and Bakri Balloon.
Need to have Obstetric Cream on the PPH trolley.
Labia minora caught by the PPH Butterfly device causing pain.
Skin got caught in the device and the Dr didn't realise it:once he realised it was fine.
Preferable to Bi Manual Compression that I had before the Butterfly device was used.

I think in this case I used the Butterfly too late to help, we gave Ergometrine ,I asked for the Butterfly, it arrived 3 minutes later. Bleeding had probably (in hindsight) already settled with Bi Manual and Ergometrine.
It wasn't in for very long.
I would have liked explanation and information before its use
1st Birth but seems to have been effective.
After insertion of the Butterfly it was immediately obvious that the bleeding was from the vaginal tear.
The way the doctor explained well enough to me.

The PPH Butterfly caught some skin of the Labia Minora on insertion causing discomfort for a few seconds. She had some discomfort while it was insitu describing it as 'burning' but was happy to continue. There was some delay with insertion as no Hibitane in the room. I advise you ensure Hibitane is on the PPH/Forceps trolley or even in the box.
Labia minora caught on insertion of the PPH Butterfly.
Vaginal pack for bleeding at Episiotomy site.
The consent process was during a contraction

Woman was comfortable with insertion, pressure and removal. I offered to show her it before insertion but she declined, but was very happy for it to be used. The end of the bed was still on and she was lying semi-recumbent. As a result of this the Butterfly was not in the optimal position and the platform was too posterior for adequate pressure. I advise that the Butterfly training advises lying the woman flat before use, and suggest lithotomy for optimal pressure.
It was preferable to a hand
Easy to use. Helped to diagnose bleeding as I was not sure if PPH was atony or trauma.
Easy to insert. Patient coped with insertion very well.
This is the first time I've used it on a patient without analgesia, it worked surprisingly well.
Feels more comfortable than the hand.
Syntocinon 5 i.u. IV and Syntocinon 10 i.u. IV
Much easier to use than I anticipated and with Bi Manual Compression.
Better than a 'hand' (had Bimanual Compression prior to the Butterfly device being inserted).
Urticarial rash onset 2/7 P/N thought to be due to Fragmin.Not admitted treated as outpatient.
Easy to use and well tolerated
1 x swob in situ from delivery room -> theatre
Much less painful than manual approach.
Had to be re catheterised when catheter removed post delivery.
Episiotomy breakdown/infection at 8/7 P/N.Treated as outpatient,reviewed 1/52 later and discharged from hospital care.
More pleasant for patient rather than Bimanual for 5 minutes.
Noted something protuding from vagina, Diagnosis of prolapse. Advised to do pelvic floor exercises.
When being recruited I overheard some discussion about whether to use the Butterfly or not which made me feel anxious/involved in something uncertain.

Discussed with Dr Mark Omar (09/11/18 at 0930). Device inserted, but handles not brought together as urethral oedema/anterior vaginal wall kept dropping between the handles. Anxious about causing trauma, attempted to manipulate over 1 minute but no success so device removed. No compression of uterus. No trauma sustained.
It didn't work as it needed to be removed due to entrapment of genitalia.
Possibly. Had a EUA under GA and sustained a small right vaginal wall graze requiring 1 suture. ? caused by Butterfly device or by EUA.
Butterfly device was used in error as the circumstances did not meet the inclusion criteria ( <1 hour and mode of delivery LSCS).
Small right vaginal wall graze noted after examination under anaesthetic and removal of clots. Required 1 suture.
Small right vaginal wall graze noted after examination under anaesthetic and removal of clots. Required 1 suture.

Although the Butterfly seemed to arrest bleeding injury initially, There was some clot in the uterus which led to continued bleeding after removal of the Butterfly, this settled once the clot was removed.
This patient only had a pudendal block and local infiltration, but tolerated it well.
vaginal examination to expel blood clots
The anterior vaginal wall of this patient made it difficult to see clearly where bleeding was coming from.
woman readmitted to LWH within 6 weeks of PPH device being used. Diagnosed with pelvic infection, treated with IV antibiotics

Returned to Liverpool Women's Hospital on the 28th and 29th November, 2018 (12 days P/N ) with signs and symptoms of pelvic infection. Admitted as an in patient on the 29th November and treated with IV antibiotics.

Discussed with Dr Puru (also present at time of device use). Device removed after 6 minutes as some on going bleeding despite compression with the device. Examination to exclude traumatic cause- none found so device re-inserted and compression continued for a further 3 minutes. Discussion with user Dr Ben Twist. The device gave him control over the situation and stopped the bleeding almost completely. Could feel well contracted uterus on the end of the device, became tired so handed over to Dr Puru.Small amount of on going loss so device removed, clot (+) on platform removed. No tears seen on inspection therefore device replaced and bleeding stopped. Impression was atonic uterus, ?? cervical tear.
It did not hurt internally only externally.
Nothing in particular. I was very "out of it" at the time
Patient consented to Butterfly prior to transfer to theatre in the event of needing a General Anaesthetic.
1 x 5 i.u. IV and 1x10 i.u. IV

Had a blood loss of 600 ml prior to insertion of device, after 1st insertion and removal,100 mls of clots removed. Still amount of Atonia with intermittent bleed- Bleeding settled after 2nd time removal.
I did not like the way the Doc. did it.
I didn't like the cuts I had on the external.
It helped to compress my uterus
It was better than a male doctor doing it.
I think in this case the retained products were causing the bleeding and no amount of Bimanual would have helped this.
